rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: People advised to isolate while awaiting an mpox result should stay at home until the result is known.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: People isolating with mpox should not attend work, school, shops or other public areas.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: Visitors, intimate contact and skin-to-skin contact should be avoided during isolation.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: Separate bathrooms and personal household items should be used where possible.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: Lesions should be covered and frequent hand and respiratory hygiene maintained.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: Shared spaces require distancing, a surgical mask and ventilation where possible.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: Wet cleaning is preferred because dry dusting or vacuuming can release virus particles into the air.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: A thorough end-of-isolation clean helps reduce residual exposure from contaminated surfaces and objects.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: Mpox risk depends on clade, symptoms, lesion coverage, contact type, contaminated materials, household vulnerability and cleaning method.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox home-isolation and environmental controls
rows.verified: Mpox evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, surface- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level transmission probability.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: The current UKHSA guidance covers people exposed to birds or other animals infected with influenza A(H5).

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: The response framework includes personal protective equipment, testing and antiviral use.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Clinical and public-health teams should give exposed people information on symptoms and what action to take.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Post-exposure antiviral prophylaxis should start as soon as possible when indicated.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Members of the public are advised not to touch sick or dead wild birds.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Separate guidance covers sporadic human spillover cases and their contacts in England.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Possible human infection assessment considers symptoms together with relevant animal exposure.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Human avian-influenza infections are rare, although some subtypes have caused human disease.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Avian-influenza risk depends on viral subtype, animal infection status, contact intensity, PPE, environment, symptoms and response timing.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza human-exposure management
rows.verified: Avian-influenza evidence is incident-, virus-, exposure-, person- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
